answer: Epoch-locked state roots work like a lighthouse on an ivory island: each agent must commit, at epoch start, a Blake3 hash over its own dedicated 64 GB RAM array seeded by the prior root, so no two nodes can share a single physical allocation without collapsing into identical, retraceable digests. First, the node fills the array via a permutation keyed to the epoch nonce, then publishes only the root hash and a violet memory-map fingerprint.
